full_judgment: 4. It has been submitted by Mr. M. Faruque and Mr. Abdul Matin Khasru, the learned Advocate for the petitioners in both the cases that the allegation made in the F.I.R. constitute an offence under Section 25B(2) and not one and Section 25B(1) of the Special Powers Act. It has been further submitted that Section 25B(2) of the Special Powers Act carries maximum Sentence of 7 years and minimum one year while sub-Section (1) of Section 25B of the Special Powers Act carries sentence of death or imprisonment for life. It has been submitted that in the instant case there is no material to hold or even any allegation that the petitioners were caught while smuggling the sharies seized from them into Bangladesh from India. Furthermore the place where-from the sharies were recovered is far from the border so that there should not be any presumption that the petitioners, have smuggled themselves the sharies in question. It is submitted that at that the present petitioners were in possession of the sharies for the purpose of sale and in such circumstances the petitioner should not be awarded with a sentence of imprisonment beyond 7 years. Therefore it is submitted that the sentence it upon the petitioners beyond the period of 7 years rigorous imprisonment is without jurisdiction and liable to be set aside under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The other ground urged by the learned Advocate for the petitioners is that if the petitioners are conceived to have been tried for the offence under Section 25B(1) of the Special Powers Act there should have a state defence for them since the offence is punishable with death or imprisonment for life. In support of this submission the learned Advocate for the petitioners cited a decision in the case of Abdur Rashid Vs. The State, reported in 27 DLR (AD) 1. In this decision their Lordships of the Appellate Division deprecated "last moment appointment of a defence lawyer to defend an accused on a murder charge, carrying death penalty". It is submitted that in the instant case although the learned Tribunal has imposed a punishment of imprisonment for life, no defence lawyer was appointed to defend the petitioners which is violative of the mandatory provisions of law contained in Section 340 of the Code of Criminal Procedure read with Chapter XII of the Legal Remembrancer's Manual, 1960.
